section: India's national accounts - NSO/MoSPI, base year revisions, quarterly estimates, informal sector estimation
subsections: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.tq: Use the first and last base years and then verify the middle sequence.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s: In national income accounting, a base year is best understood as the year whose prices are used to:
o: Measure only the volume of exports
Determine the annual rate of population growth
Calculate only nominal GDP at current prices
Value real GDP at constant prices
accepted.x: The base year is the reference year whose prices are used to value real GDP at constant prices. For an index, the base year is generally assigned a value of 100.
accepted.tq: Distinguish constant-price valuation from current-price valuation.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the revision of base years:
1. A base year should ideally be revised every five years.
2. In practice, revisions have generally occurred at intervals of five to ten years.
3. Revision helps capture changes in the composition of output and relative prices.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Periodic revision makes the estimates more representative of changing production patterns and relative prices.
accepted.tq: Test the ideal rule, practical trend and purpose together.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s: The new series of National Accounts Statistics with base 2022-23 was released by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation on:
accepted.x: The NSO, MoSPI released the new 2022-23 base series on 27 February 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the precise release date from nearby years and dates.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s: The new national accounts series with base 2022-23 includes annual and quarterly estimates covering which period?
accepted.x: The new series provides annual and quarterly estimates for the period from 2022-23 to 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Match the coverage period with the correct base-series release.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s: The 2022-23 base year series of national accounts follows which edition of the United Nations System of National Accounts?
accepted.x: The 2022-23 series follows the United Nations System of National Accounts, 2025 edition.
accepted.tq: Use the exact institutional standard rather than a neighbouring edition.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s: Why was 2022-23 considered a suitable base year for the revised national accounts series?
o: It was selected because base years cannot be revised after five years.
It was the first year in which India adopted the 2008 SNA.
It represented the peak of the COVID-related economic contraction.
It was unaffected by the GST transition, the COVID period and the immediate base effects of 2021-22.
accepted.x: 2022-23 was treated as a relatively normal year; 2017-18 involved the GST transition, 2019-21 was affected by COVID, and 2021-22 carried base effects.
accepted.tq: Identify the normal-year rationale by eliminating crisis and transition years.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: GDP and national accounts have the new base 2022-23, replacing 2011-12. CPI has base 2024, merchandise trade indices have base 2022-23, and IIP has base 2022-23.
accepted.tq: Compare the base-year rows and detect the swapped index.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s:
With reference to the revised index-number series, consider the following statements:
1. The CPI has base 2024.
2. The old CPI base was calendar year 2012.
3. The old CPI base was 2011-12.
4. Merchandise trade indices have base 2022-23, replacing 2012-13.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The old CPI base was calendar year 2012, not financial year 2011-12.
accepted.tq: Catch the confusable calendar-year and financial-year distinction.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s: The Index of Industrial Production, after rebasing, is released:
accepted.x: The IIP was rebased to 2022-23 and is released monthly with a 28-day lag.
accepted.tq: Pair the frequency with the precise release lag.
accepted.sec: Base year revisions - sequence, current base, next revision

accepted.s: Who made the first attempt to estimate India's national income in 1868 in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India?
accepted.x: Dadabhai Naoroji made the first recorded attempt in 1868 and estimated per capita income at Rs 20.
accepted.tq: Link the pioneering estimate with its author and year.

accepted.s: Dadabhai Naoroji's 1868 estimate placed India's per capita income at approximately:
accepted.x: Dadabhai Naoroji estimated India's per capita income at Rs 20 in 1868. Some accounts also associate his estimate with 1876, but the estimate value given is Rs 20.
accepted.tq: Distinguish close historical estimates by their exact numerical value.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

a. William Digby — 1899 — Rs 18
b. Findlay Shirras — 1911 — Rs 49
c. Wadia and Joshi — 1913-14 — Rs 44.30
d. Dadabhai Naoroji — 1868 — Rs 20
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. William Digby estimated per capita income at Rs 18 in 1899; Shirras Rs 49 in 1911; Wadia and Joshi Rs 44.30 in 1913-14; and Naoroji Rs 20 in 1868.
accepted.tq: Start with a sure author-year pair and verify each numerical value.

accepted.s: Dr V.K.R.V. Rao's national income estimate for 1925-29 placed per capita income at:
accepted.x: Dr V.K.R.V. Rao's estimate placed per capita income at Rs 76.
accepted.tq: Use the estimator-value association rather than the chronological order alone.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Income Committee:
1. It was constituted in August 1949.
2. It was chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis.
3. D.R. Gadgil and V.K.R.V. Rao were members.
4. Its first report was issued in 1951.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The committee was constituted in August 1949, chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis, included Gadgil and Rao, and submitted its first report in 1951.
accepted.tq: Combine constitution, composition and report-year facts in one coded question.

accepted.s: The first official estimate of national income for 1948-49 reported by the National Income Committee was:
o: National income Rs 7,610 crore and per capita income Rs 225
National income Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income Rs 49
National income Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income Rs 225
National income Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income Rs 76
accepted.x: The first official estimate reported national income for 1948-49 as Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income as Rs 225.
accepted.tq: Keep the aggregate and per-capita figures paired correctly.

accepted.s: The National Income Committee's first official estimate related to which accounting year?
accepted.x: The first official estimate of the National Income Committee related to 1948-49 and was presented in its 1951 report.
accepted.tq: Separate the reference year from the year of publication.

accepted.s: The Central Statistical Office has prepared national income estimates since:
accepted.x: The CSO has prepared national income estimates since 1955. Some accounts mention 1954 in connection with its institutional history, but the stated year for preparation of estimates is 1955.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the institutional formation year from the year of commencing estimates.

accepted.s: The National Statistical Office (NSO) was formed through the merger of:
o: NSC and State Directorates of Economics and Statistics
accepted.x: The NSO was formed in 2019 by merging the Central Statistical Office and the National Sample Survey Office under MoSPI.
accepted.tq: Identify the two constituent organisations rather than the supervising ministry or advisory body.

accepted.s: The National Statistical Office functions under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
accepted.x: The NSO functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, abbreviated as MoSPI.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-organisation association carefully.

accepted.s: The NSO is headed by the:
o: Chairperson of the National Statistical Commission
Secretary of the Ministry of Finance
accepted.x: The NSO is headed by the Chief Statistician of India. The office is described as carrying the rank of Chief Secretary, and the Chief Statistician is also Secretary, MoSPI.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the executive head of NSO from the advisory statistical commission.

accepted.s:
Which of the following is NOT among the functions or outputs associated with the NSO?

1. Compilation of national accounts
2. Compilation of the IIP
3. Compilation of CPI for rural, urban and combined sectors
4. Conduct of field surveys such as PLFS, ASUSE and HCES
5. Formulation of monetary policy

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 to 4 describe NSO-related functions, including national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys. Formulation of monetary policy is not an NSO function.
accepted.tq: Find the activity belonging to a different policy authority.

accepted.s: The Index of Industrial Production data are compiled from how many source agencies?
accepted.x: IIP data are obtained from 14 source agencies and released on the 28th of each month.
accepted.tq: Use the exact count associated with the statistical compilation process.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. National Accounts Division — GDP, consumption and capital formation
2. Economic Statistics Division — IIP
3. Industrial Statistics Wing, Kolkata — ASI
4. National Statistical Office — National Industrial Classification

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. The National Accounts Division handles GDP, consumption and capital formation; ESD compiles IIP; the Kolkata wing conducts ASI; and NSO compiles the National Industrial Classification.
accepted.tq: Match each division or body with its specific statistical output.

accepted.s:
Which of the following activities is primarily associated with the old NSSO component of the NSO?

1. Periodic Labour Force Survey
2. Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises
3. Household Consumption Expenditure Survey
4. Preparation of annual National Accounts Statistics

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: PLFS, ASUSE and HCES are field surveys conducted by the NSS component. Preparation of annual National Accounts Statistics is associated with the National Accounts Division.
accepted.tq: Separate field-survey functions from national-accounts compilation.

accepted.s: The National Statistical Commission, established in 2006, consists of:
o: The MoSPI Secretary and the four Chief Statisticians of India
A full-time Chairperson and four full-time members
A part-time Chairperson and two full-time members
A part-time Chairperson and four part-time members
accepted.x: The NSC consists of a part-time Chairperson and four part-time members. The CEO of NITI Aayog is an ex officio member and the MoSPI Secretary is its Secretary.
accepted.tq: Test the composition separately from ex officio membership and secretarial roles.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the National Statistical Commission is correct?

1. The CEO of NITI Aayog is an ex officio member.
2. The Secretary of MoSPI serves as its Secretary.
3. It is the nodal body for statistical standards.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The NSC is the nodal body for statistical standards, includes the CEO of NITI Aayog ex officio, and has the MoSPI Secretary as its Secretary.
accepted.tq: Combine composition, office-holding and institutional role in coded form.

accepted.s: The Central Statistical Office was formed on 2 May 1951 as the:
accepted.x: The CSO was formed on 2 May 1951 as the Central Statistical Institute and was merged into the CSO in 1954.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original institutional name from its later organisational form.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

A. NSO — umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys
B. NSC — State Domestic Product compiler
C. ISI — department directly under MoSPI
D. State DES — national-level monetary policy authority
o: NSO — umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys
State DES — national-level monetary policy authority
accepted.x: The NSO is the umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys. State DES prepares State Domestic Product and state statistics, while ISI is autonomous under the ISI Act, 1959.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly assigned institutional role among swapped bodies.

accepted.s: The Industrial Statistics Wing located at Kolkata is associated with conducting the:
accepted.x: The Industrial Statistics Wing at Kolkata conducts the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI).
accepted.tq: Link the location-specific wing with its survey responsibility.

accepted.s: Which institution is autonomous under the ISI Act, 1959?
accepted.x: The Indian Statistical Institute is an autonomous institution under the ISI Act, 1959.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an autonomous statutory institution from government statistical bodies.

accepted.s: State Directorates of Economics and Statistics are primarily associated with the preparation of:
o: State Domestic Product and state statistics
National Accounts Statistics and IIP for the Union
The United Nations System of National Accounts
accepted.x: State DES prepare State Domestic Product and other state-level statistics. National-level accounts and IIP are compiled through the NSO and its divisions.
accepted.tq: Assign the statistical task according to the level of government.
